name: Convento de San Marcos, León (concentration camp)
story: León fell to the rebels in the first days of the war, and the vast Renaissance monastery of San Marcos was turned into one of the largest prison camps in Spain. Thousands of men — and women in a separate section — from León, Asturias and the Northern front were crowded into its halls and stables, with many taken out for execution or dying of disease. The same building had been a pilgrim hospital on the Camino de Santiago; today it is a luxury Parador, and survivors' associations have long pressed for proper recognition of its prison past.
see: The famous Plateresque façade on the Bernesga river, the church and cloister (museum); the hotel interior is not a memorial site.
plan: Façade free; the church/museum section (Museo de León) is free too (check hours). Be aware the building's prison history is barely signposted.

boxes.text: Prisoner totals and deaths vary between sources. Figures such as 'up to 7,000 at a time' appear in some accounts but are not confirmed here.
